html:
Stoicism is a school of philosophy founded in Athens around 300 BCE by Zeno of Citium. He taught in the Stoa Poikile, the Painted Porch on the Agora, which gave the school its name.

Zeno had studied with the Cynic Crates. The Stoics taught that the world is ordered by reason, the logos, and that a good life means living in agreement with it. Virtue is the only true good; wealth, health and fame are not. Most suffering comes from false judgments, so we should change what we can and calmly accept what we cannot. All people share in reason, so all are citizens of one world.

Chrysippus, the school's third head, built it into a full system of logic, physics and ethics. Its rival was Epicureanism.

Stoicism became the favourite philosophy of educated Romans. Cicero spread its ideas, and its best known writers are Roman: the statesman Seneca, the former slave Epictetus and the emperor Marcus Aurelius, whose Meditations are still widely read. It shaped Christian ethics and the idea of natural law, and modern talking therapies draw on it.
